title: The Sweet Harbor
premise: Casper Almeida, a pastry chef whose Sweet Harbor café is three missed payments from foreclosure, is roped into her town's anonymous pen-pal festival by the library board — and discovers her assigned correspondent is Theo Marchetti, the rival baker whose family she blames for her father's death twelve years ago. As their letters strip away old grievances and a shared recipe notebook surfaces suggesting both families were deceived by a third party, Casper must choose between the loyalty that has defined her grief and the truth that could save both their businesses. At the harbor festival's final night, she publicly forgives herself for the accident she believes she caused, confesses to Theo, and together they merge their struggling cafés into one — with the festival's prize money keeping the doors open.
about_author: Mirabel Joubert is a former pastry cook who traded early mornings in a bakery kitchen for early mornings at a writing desk in a coastal town much like the one she left behind. She writes romances about people who rebuild themselves out of flour, salt water, and second chances.

chapters.title: Three Payments Left
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Opening on a failing ledger and a perfect lemon tart, Casper counts down her café's last weeks while deflecting her landlord's notice. Emotional beat: weary defiance masking fear.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Assignment
chapters.summary: The library board's pen-pal festival pairs townsfolk anonymously; Casper signs up half-jokingly for the marketing exposure. Her first letter goes out unsigned. Beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Flour and Grudges
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rival baker Theo Marchetti receives his assignment and vents about his own failing shop — never guessing his correspondent is Casper, whose letters already unsettle him. Beat: prickly curiosity.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Salt
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the dock accident that killed Casper's father, the Marchetti boat involved, and the silence between the families since. Casper's POV. Beat: buried grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: Letters Without Faces
chapters.summary: The correspondence deepens; both confess business fears they'd never say aloud. Casper realizes she's telling a stranger what she can't tell anyone. Beat: intimacy without identity.

chapters.title: The Recipe Notebook
chapters.summary: Casper finds her father's old recipe notebook containing a page in a Marchetti hand — a collaboration neither family ever mentioned. Beat: the ground shifts under her certainty.

chapters.title: Health Inspector
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. An anonymous complaint triggers an inspection at Theo's shop; he suspects sabotage and hardens toward his unknown rival. Beat: paranoia tightening the noose.

chapters.title: Almost Meeting
chapters.summary: A near-miss at the post office where each almost recognizes the other's handwriting. Casper's POV, laced with dramatic irony. Beat: suspense and denial.

chapters.title: Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Both are drafted onto the harbor festival committee and forced to work side by side, trading barbs that feel increasingly like flirtation. Alternating POVs. Beat: enemies softening.

chapters.title: What the Letters Know
chapters.summary: Casper notices her pen pal describes details only someone inside the Marchetti bakery would know. Her suspicion curdles into dread. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Reveal
chapters.summary: Midpoint climax: comparing handwriting on festival signage, Casper confirms Theo is her correspondent — and storms out before he can explain. Beat: betrayal, heartbreak, fury.

chapters.title: Burnt Sugar
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He confronts Casper; she throws the accident at him. He reveals he was a child then too, and that he signed up hoping to finally earn forgiveness. Beat: raw confrontation.

chapters.title: Foreclosure Notice
chapters.summary: The bank letter arrives; Casper hides it from everyone, working herself hollow. A quiet chapter of isolation where pride costs her allies. Beat: rock bottom approaching.

chapters.title: Nadia's Testimony
chapters.summary: Theo's aunt Nadia admits the Marchettis knew the dock mooring had been tampered with and stayed silent out of fear of the harbormaster — the third party both families trusted. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallized.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper and Theo, uneasy allies now, dig through marina records and find proof the harbormaster falsified inspection logs after taking kickbacks. Beat: purpose forged from pain.

chapters.title: Confession in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Casper admits to Theo the truth she's never said: she was supposed to check the moorings that day and didn't. His forgiveness terrifies her more than blame. Beat: the enemy in the mirror named.

chapters.title: Sabotage at Midnight
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the café and steals the recipe notebook; evidence points to the harbormaster protecting himself. Stakes turn criminal. Beat: rising danger.

chapters.title: All Hands
chapters.summary: The found-family network — library board, Nadia, regulars, even rival staff — rallies to restore the café before the festival. Beat: warmth earned through crisis.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: At the festival opening, the pair presents the ledger evidence publicly; the harbormaster is confronted and the town's twelve-year story breaks open. Beat: cathartic climax, part one.

chapters.title: Forgive the Mirror
chapters.summary: Alone at dawn on the dock, Casper reads her father's last unsent letter to her and finally forgives herself. She writes her pen pal one last honest letter — signed. Beat: emotional climax.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Theo reads her confession onstage during the festival's finale as the prize is announced; their joint entry wins, saving both shops if they merge. He answers aloud. Beat: love declared in public.

chapters.title: One Sign, Two Names
chapters.summary: Epilogue weeks later: the merged café opens under a new sign, the notebook restored to its wall, letters framed behind the counter. Casper's POV closing on chosen family and unburdened memory. Beat: resolution and hope.
